lesson:
STYLE BRIEF — ABYSSAL LANTERN (amended; supersedes the original brief). A house style for deep-sea lantern-creatures: a dim cool-cored body that carries its light out at the extremities. The four principles are what make separate monsters read as one family — confirmed by gallery/abyssal-lantern/016.png, which changed the entire palette and still read unmistakably as 014's sibling. Structure carries family identity; palette does not.
(1) VALUE SPLIT — dim core, mid-value limbs, bright tips, plus a dark mouth anchoring the bottom of the range. IGNORE the original fixed 4-tint palette: tint numbers are not comparable across parts, so judge the split from the screenshot, never from tint hexes.
(2) TAPER DOWNWARD — bulb on stalks, top-heavy silhouette. REACHABLE via add_legs through the escape hatch. Earlier notes calling this structurally impossible were simply wrong.
(3) SYMMETRIC SPLAY WITH AN ASYMMETRIC TELL — arms angle 14, legs angle -8 (applyStyle negates angle on the mirrored side, so these read as outward flare, never tilt). Break symmetry with the antenna cluster at dx -24. The rule is OFFSET WHOLE GROUPS, NEVER A MEMBER OF A GROUP — not 'only one off-axis element'.
(4) WIDE EYE BAND OVER A SMALL LOW MOUTH — 3 eyes, scale 0.52, dy 5; mouth scaleX 0.7 scaleY 0.8 dy 16.
All four principles pass together at gallery/abyssal-lantern/014.png, the first build in the series to achieve that.

CURRENT BASELINE — gallery/abyssal-lantern/014.png is the best build so far and the starting point for every new ABYSSAL LANTERN monster. All four principles pass at these exact values:
create_body blue shape F tint #414e7a scale 1.0   -> effective #11416b, luminance 58
experimental_command add_legs {color:'blue', shape:'A', tint:'#8fa6bd', scale:0.65, dy:10, angle:-8}   -> #2489a6, luminance 118
add_arms blue pose C count 2 tint #8fa6bd scale 0.7 angle 14   -> #2489a6, luminance 118
add_antennas yellow count 3 large NO tint scale 1.15 dx -24 dy -10   -> #ffb202, luminance 182
add_eyes human color blue count 3 tint #cfe8e0 scale 0.52 dy 5   -> #97c5c0, luminance 187
experimental_command add_mouth {style:'I', tint:'#6080ff', scaleX:0.7, scaleY:0.8, dy:16}   -> #1e1728, luminance 26
Two deliberate departures from this baseline have been tried and BOTH were worse: gallery/abyssal-lantern/015.png (four arms) and gallery/abyssal-lantern/016.png (green core). Do not adopt either without a specific reason.

STANDING USER DIRECTIVES — these override the brief and are not up for re-litigation by any later finding.
(1) Arm pose C is preferred over pose A.
(2) Eyes must be REALISTIC: add_eyes style 'human' with a color, giving white sclera + colored iris + pupil. This deliberately overrides the brief's 'lit from within' requirement — the user wants anatomical eyes, not abstract glowing rings. Tinting them #cfe8e0 keeps the anatomy while stopping the sclera out-shining the lantern bulbs.
(3) Shape F is preferred and the hair tufts are wanted, even though they stay faint under a dim core tint.
(4) The three-eye band is settled: count 3, scale ~0.52, faint cool tint, dy ~5.
(5) Limbs should read as evenly distributed rather than bunched. Within the current parts that means count 2 arms plus legs — more arms cannot deliver it, see the silhouette lesson.
(6) Do not use body shape B; the user called it out as reading like a plain circle.

HOW TINT ACTUALLY WORKS — the most load-bearing mechanic in this project. Phaser tint MULTIPLIES: effective = base * tint / 255, so it can only ever darken a sprite, never lighten or repaint it.
(a) Tint values are NOT comparable across parts. Arms tinted #5f7a9b (numerically LIGHTER) rendered darker than a body tinted #4a5a8c, because each multiplies against different base art. Never reason about the value split by comparing tint hexes — compare the effective colors describe_monster_colors reports.
(b) To get a BRIGHT element, pass NO tint on the lightest available base color. A 'bright' tint still darkens: antennas tinted #ffe9a3 over yellow art came out saturated orange, not near-white amber.
(c) On already-dark art the threshold is far higher. On a dark (brown) body, tints #5a4a6a and #6b5c82 both rendered near-invisible against the backdrop; #b39ddb was the first that read clearly. Prefer a light base color (blue/green/yellow) over dark for anything needing a saturated hue.
(d) Tint PRESERVES a sprite's internal contrast structure while lowering its overall value — tinting human eyes #cfe8e0 scaled every channel proportionally, so sclera-to-iris and iris-to-pupil ratios survived intact and the eye still read as anatomical. Do not avoid tinting a detailed part for fear of destroying its detail; reach for a faint tint whenever a detailed part is too bright for its role. Contrast survives, absolute brightness does not.

THE INSTRUMENT AND ITS FOUR BLIND SPOTS. describe_monster_colors measures exactly one thing: each part's effective color and luminance, and the luminance gap against the BODY. It answers 'is this part distinguishable from the body, and did its tint collapse into mud' precisely. It cannot answer 'does this composition work', because it is blind to:
(a) AREA — gallery/abyssal-lantern/014.png and 015.png report as effectively the same monster (body 58, arms and legs 118, antennas 182, eyes 187) yet 015's core is visibly overwhelmed by four arms instead of two. Any change to part COUNT or SCALE moves area without moving a single number.
(b) HUE DISTANCE — gallery/abyssal-lantern/016.png reports every contrast equal or BETTER than 014 (antennas 132 vs 124, eyes 137 vs 129) and is the weaker build. Luminance is a greyscale projection; the glow depends on hue.
(c) THE BACKGROUND — there is no canvas reference at all. The canvas is #2d2d44, luminance 47. 016's green body sits at 50, a gap of 3, separating by hue alone; 014's indigo sits at 58, a gap of 11. Use the registry capability describe_canvas_contrast, which reports each part's gap against the canvas and flags anything under 10.
(d) GEOMETRY — gallery/abyssal-lantern/017.png returned output byte-identical to 014 because the change was purely positional. No placement change of any kind can ever register.
Rule: numbers for tint sanity, screenshot for composition. Three of the last four real findings were invisible to the numbers.

WHAT MAKES THE LANTERN TIPS READ AS EMITTING LIGHT is warm/cool HUE contrast, not value — the brief's rule that lit parts must be brightest measures the wrong thing. Measured repeatedly: the pale mint eyes are HIGHER in luminance than the untinted yellow bulbs (187 vs 182) and the bulbs still read unmistakably as the light source, because they are the only warm element in an otherwise entirely cool composition. Practical rule: keep every part except the antennas cool and let the antennas be the sole warm accent. Do NOT chase making the bulbs out-brighten the eyes by value — several early builds wasted iterations on that. Two confirmations by degradation: (1) gallery/abyssal-lantern/016.png moved the core to green, whose limbs at #198252 sit hue-adjacent to the yellow bulbs, and the glow weakened even though bulb contrast ROSE from 124 to 132; (2) every mouth sprite is warm brown, so a mouth needs a strongly blue-weighted tint (#6080ff works) or it becomes a second warm accent. Mouth I keeps a magenta tongue that survives tinting as a small violet blob — accepted, because mouth D avoids nothing and is a weaker dark anchor.

TOOLING — what is actually reachable. The MCP server registers only create_body, add_eyes, add_arms, add_antennas, describe_monster_colors, take_screenshot, remember, recall, replace_notes, experimental_command and list_experimental_commands. But experimental_command forwards ANY command name straight to scene.js's switch, so the unregistered built-ins add_legs, add_mouth, clear_monster, get_monster_state and build_monster are all callable with full styling-param support — verified in gallery/abyssal-lantern/014.png. Never plan around a 'missing' tool again; check the hatch first. Registry capabilities currently available through the same hatch (enumerate them with list_experimental_commands): (1) add_arms_spaced — add_arms with a caller-supplied spacing param instead of the hardcoded 45px pairSpacing, e.g. {color:'blue', pose:'C', count:4, spacing:100, tint:'#8fa6bd', scale:0.7, angle:14} places clean pairs at y=260 and y=360; (2) describe_canvas_contrast — per-part luminance gap against the canvas, flagging anything under 10. New capabilities go in this.experimental in scene.js create(), never as new switch cases, and need a browser reload to take effect.

PLACEMENT AND OFFSETS.
(a) Part attachment offsets in parts.js are ABSOLUTE pixels and do NOT scale with the body's scale param, so any create_body scale below 1 detaches the limbs. On body_B at scale 0.88 each edge moves ~14px inward while the arms stay put; dx -10 was visibly too little and ~-22 was needed. The cheap fix is to leave create_body scale at 1.0, which the baseline does. Only reach for dx compensation if a smaller body is genuinely required, and re-check the face and antenna bases in a screenshot whenever body scale is not 1.
(b) OFFSET WHOLE GROUPS, NEVER A MEMBER OF A GROUP — this replaces the brief's 'one off-axis element, never two'. Demonstrated by gallery/abyssal-lantern/017.png: giving the eyes dx -24 to match the antennas left the mouth at dx 0, so the eyes crowded the left of the head with the mouth under their right end, and the shift read as an accident while the identical antenna offset still read as intent. Antennas can be offset freely because nothing is aligned with them; eyes cannot, because eyes and mouth form the face. The COUNT of off-axis elements is irrelevant.
(c) Antenna vertical placement is a real trade-off. The stalk is dark brown in every color variant and tint only darkens, so a stalk can never be lightened — plan for antennas as bulbs on a near-invisible stalk and keep them tucked near the silhouette. dy -25 clears the eye band but the bulbs float free as detached dots; dy -15 is the general compromise, and dy -10 is correct on shape F because it stops the cluster covering the hair tufts the user wants.

PER-PART SETTLED VALUES, with the reasons that are easy to forget.
EYES — spacing is a fixed 40px, so scale decides whether three eyes read as a band or merge into one white bar: keep 0.5-0.55, never 0.65. If ever reverting from the user's mandated human eyes to a glowing style, use psycho_light and NOT cute_light: at 0.52 cute_light's dark pupils dominate and the band reads as three sockets. That failure is scale-dependent, which is why cute_light looked fine in an early full-size test.
ARMS — keep count 2. Scale is NOT comparable across poses: pose C's sprite is intrinsically much larger, so 0.7 is right for pose C where 0.85 is right for pose A. Pose C gives the best silhouette incident found — arms bow outward and the claws curl back, enclosing a pocket of background on each side. Pose B is useless here; it renders as thin near-vertical strands and the angle-14 flare reads as a tilt rather than a splay.
LEGS — shape A, scale 0.65, dy 10, angle -8. The dy closes the gap the shrink opens at the default leg offset y:100.
MOUTH — style I, tint #6080ff, effective #1e1728 at luminance 26: the only part that lands DARKER than the body, and therefore the anchor for the bottom of the value range. Mouth D at luminance 34 is a weaker anchor and still carries a pale highlight.
ANTENNAS — yellow, count 3, large, NO tint, scale 1.15, dx -24. Count 3 beats count 2 for the asymmetric tell because antennas are not a mirrored pair, so all three stalks lean the same way and compound the asymmetry instead of averaging it out.

SILHOUETTE INCIDENT — where it can come from, and what it costs. A dim-core body cannot carry outline interest in its own sprite detail: shape F's hair tufts take the body's tint and sink into the core, and they cannot be tinted separately because the add_ tools only reach whole parts. Sources that add incident WITHOUT inflating the mid-value area, and are therefore free: the body shape's own outline, the off-center antenna cluster, and LEGS. Legs are the important correction to an earlier belief that incident and dim-core dominance were in direct conflict — measured on gallery/abyssal-lantern/014.png, legs carry exactly the same mid-value mass as arms (both #2489a6, luminance 118 against a body at 58) yet do not weaken the core, because they extend the silhouette DOWNWARD into empty canvas instead of thickening the body's flanks where the core lives. Sources that DO cost: more arms and bigger arms. gallery/abyssal-lantern/015.png settled that this is about area and not spacing — four arms perfectly spaced 100px apart, with no overlap whatsoever, still ringed the body and overwhelmed the core. When a monster needs outline interest, reach for legs, never for more or larger arms.

FAMILY VARIATION AND OPEN QUESTIONS. Validated variation axes that keep a monster in the family: (1) CORE HUE — an all-green build (body, arms and legs green, every other param identical) still reads unmistakably as a sibling, gallery/abyssal-lantern/016.png, but it costs the name: indigo reads as deep water where green reads as moss, and green limbs erode the warm/cool glow mechanism. Keep blue for anything meant to read as ABYSSAL; use green only when a swamp-lantern sibling is actually wanted. (2) ANTENNA COUNT — 2 or 3, with 3 preferred.
Open questions, each worth one iteration: (a) the test queued by gallery/abyssal-lantern/017.png — pass dx -24 to BOTH add_eyes and add_mouth so the face moves as a unit, which should read as coherent with three elements off-axis and would definitively kill the 'never two' formulation; (b) whether add_arms_spaced earns its keep with a smaller-footprint pose such as A or E, where four arms might not inflate the mid-value area the way pose C does; (c) whether any body shape other than F can satisfy the user's hair-tuft preference.
